english: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be the angles of a triangle such that $\cot A+\cot B+\cot C=\dfrac52$. Then the value of $\operatorname{cosec}^2A+\operatorname{cosec}^2B+\operatorname{cosec}^2C$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A$, $B$ तथा $C$ एक त्रिभुज के कोण हैं जिनके लिए $\cot A+\cot B+\cot C=\dfrac52$ है। तब $\operatorname{cosec}^2A+\operatorname{cosec}^2B+\operatorname{cosec}^2C$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $A+B=\pi-C\Rightarrow\cot(A+B)=-\cot C\Rightarrow\dfrac{\cot A\cot B-1}{\cot A+\cot B}=-\cot C$
$\Rightarrow\cot A\cot B+\cot B\cot C+\cot C\cot A=1$
solution_full: $\cot(A+B)=\dfrac{\cot A\cot B-1}{\cot A+\cot B}$, so $\cot A\cot B-1=-\cot C(\cot A+\cot B)$, i.e. $\cot A\cot B+\cot B\cot C+\cot C\cot A=1$. (If one angle is a right angle, its cotangent is $0$ and the identity still holds.)
Squaring the given sum: $\left(\sum\cot A\right)^2=\sum\cot^2A+2\sum\cot A\cot B$, so $\sum\cot^2A=\dfrac{25}{4}-2=\dfrac{17}{4}$.
(Such triangles exist: $\cot A+\cot B+\cot C$ takes every value $\ge\sqrt3$, and $\dfrac52>\sqrt3$.)
originality_note: New: the sum of cosec^2 of the angles is a function of the sum of cotangents alone, via the conditional identity sum cot A cot B = 1 (way 4). Closest known: proving sum cot A cot B = 1 and cot A + cot B + cot C >= sqrt3. Different because: the identity is used as a tool to convert a given sum into a sum of squares, not proved.
blueprint_concepts: Conditional identities when A + B + C = pi

concept_use.Conditional identities when A + B + C =: cot A cot B + cot B cot C + cot C cot A = 1 for A + B + C = pi turns the square of the given sum into the sum of cot^2.
